claim_formal: ∀ q∈(0,4], ∀ bounded (smooth if q<1) marked Jordan domain (D;a,b), ∀ admissible lattice approximations: Law(critical square-lattice FK Dobrushin interface η_δ) ⇒ chordal SLE_{κ(q)}, κ(q)=4π/arccos(−√q/2); for 1≤q≤4 nested loops ⇒ CLE_κ

quote_A.text: critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal

quote_B.text: confirming the Rohde–Schramm prediction in this parameter range

notes: Scaling-limit identification coded M9 (limit law identified exactly); M7 is the alternative. Rohde–Schramm Conjecture 9.7 covers 0<q<4; family covers 0<q≤4 but only smooth Jordan domains for q<1 (possible O5). Corollaries: Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation, arm/thermodynamic exponents; also disordered/thermal FK-Ising and natural-measure results.

claim_formal: ∀ bounded Jordan domain D, ∀ counterclockwise marks a,b,c,d on ∂D: lim_{ε→0} P(annealed Poisson–Voronoi black crossing C_ε(D;a,b,c,d)) = F(x), F Cardy's formula

quote_A.text: \lim_{\eps\downarrow0}\PP\bigl(\mathcal C_\eps(D;a,b,c,d)\bigr) =F(x)

quote_B.text: The theorem resolves positively the annealed Cardy-crossing conjecture for critical Poisson--Voronoi percolation, the crossing-probability aspect of Schramm's Problem~2.12 above.

notes: Problem source is Schramm's 2006 problem collection (Problem 2.12, full conformal invariance); only the annealed crossing aspect is settled, hence O5 (O1 if the annealed Cardy conjecture is taken as the posed problem). Secondary: quenched near-critical universality of crossing thresholds and pivotal amplitude ~ c_V ε^{-3/4}.

claim_formal: ∀ c∈(0,2]: the balanced-torus plane state P_c of the six-vertex model (a=b=1) exists and h_δ ⇒ σ(c)Γ (plane GFF), with σ(c)^2 = 1/arcsin(c/2)

quote_A.text: converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field. For unit height jumps and Green kernel

quote_B.text: converges to a Gaussian free field, including at the endpoint c = 2

notes: No named conjecture is quoted in the input; the GFF limit for six-vertex heights is the standard prediction (P1 vs P2 uncertain). Intro mentions a 'previously untreated range', so part of the range was known: O1 for the full range, O8 is an alternative.

claim_formal: Law of complete half-plane Temperleyan double-dimer loop ensemble F(L_δ) ⇒ nested CLE_4 in ℍ as δ→0, loops matched as curves

quote_A.text: F(\mathcal L_\delta)\ \Longrightarrow\ F(\mathcal L), \qquad \delta\downarrow0, \] where \(\mathcal L\) is standard nested \(\CLE_4\) in \(\HH\)

quote_B.text: This resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer CLE4 scaling-limit conjecture.

notes: Upper half-plane Temperleyan setting only → O5 per rule 6 (O1 if that form is regarded as the posed problem). Builds on the cylindrical (lamination) convergence of [BI, Thm 4.2].

claim_formal: ∀ β∈[0,1), ∃ λ(β)>0 deterministic: with t_n = log n/(2λ(β)), ∀ε∈(0,1): worst-start TV distance d_n((1−ε)t_n)→1 and d_n((1+ε)t_n)→0 in probability over Gaussian SK disorder (cutoff)

quote_A.text: there is a deterministic \(\lambda(\beta)>0\) such that, with \[ t_n=\frac{\log n}{2\lambda(\beta)}, \]

quote_B.text: We prove worst-case total-variation cutoff for the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick heat-bath dynamics at every fixed inverse temperature

notes: Bundle: high-temp cutoff and spectral gap (β<1), critical mixing n^{2/3+o(1)} at β=1, stretched-exponential typical-start barriers for β>1, universal critical autocorrelation limits (the title result). Headline taken from the summary's lead sentence. Lean: SKHighTemperature is the β<1 spectral gap, SKRatio is cutoff only for β<1/2, others are β≥1 results, hence weaker. Problem type uncertain (fast mixing throughout high temperature is a widely expected open question; no named conjecture in the input).

claim_formal: ∃ stable radial pair potential φ on ℝ^3 (bounded continuous, |φ(r)|≤Cr^{−3−1/32}; or divergent-core variant), ∃ open density interval I, ∃ β_c: ∀ρ∈I, canonical free energy f(·,ρ) finite and D^-_β f(β_c,ρ) > D^+_β f(β_c,ρ)

quote_A.text: We construct a stable radial pair potential in three dimensions whose canonical free energy has a strict downward derivative jump at one common finite positive inverse temperature throughout an open interval of positive densities.

quote_B.text: realizing the type of transition sought in Simon's continuum problem

notes: Simon's 1984 problems in mathematical physics = numbered list, hence P3. The paper disclaims Lennard–Jones and conventional phase identification, and the first potential lacks a power-law tail margin; whether this 'settles' Simon's problem is debatable (O5 alternative). Lean RadialDensityInterval matches the bounded algebraic-decay version.

claim_formal: ∀ d,λ (3-state symmetric channel, either sign; 4-state ferromagnetic Potts) on d-ary regular trees (d≥2) and Poisson(d) GW trees: reconstruction ⇔ dλ²>1, with nonreconstruction at dλ²=1

quote_A.text: reconstruction occurs if and only if \[ d\lambda^2>1, \] with $d=b$ in the regular case. At every admissible equality $d\lambda^2=1$, there is non-reconstruction.

quote_B.text: This resolves the all-degree three-state regular-tree prediction.

notes: Exact threshold coded M9 (M5 'iff' alternative). Kesten–Stigum tightness for q=3,4 is the predicted answer. Corollary: exact weak-recovery threshold for the 3-community SBM; also an L3-capacity criterion for 4-state reconstruction. Lean covers only the supercritical (reconstruction above KS) direction, hence weaker.

claim_formal: ∀ κ∈(0,8), with h(r)=r^d(log log(1/r))^{(2−d)/2}, d=1+κ/8: almost surely ∀ 0<s<t<∞, 0 < H^h(γ[s,t]) < ∞ for chordal SLE_κ γ (and E H^h(Γ∩B(0,R)) < ∞)

quote_A.text: we construct a deterministic Hausdorff gauge that almost surely assigns positive finite measure to every nontrivial compact positive-time segment

quote_B.text: This answers Schramm's Hausdorff-measure existence problem in this parameter range.

notes: Schramm 2006 Problem 7.1 (problem collection), hence P3. The gauge is explicit (rule 1: still ∃). M9 is an alternative because the gauge is exact/sharp, and the larger gauge Schramm suggested is shown not σ-finite (corollary). Lean SLELowerPositivity is only the lower (positivity) half.

claim_formal: ∃ one Borel root-independent equivariant rule Φ, ∀ infinite connected locally finite simple graph G: {e : Φ(G,U,e)=1} with iid Uniform[0,1] labels U has law FUSF_G

quote_A.text: There is one Borel, root-independent, equivariant rule \[ \Phi(G,U,e)\in\{0,1\} \] such that, for every infinite connected locally finite simple undirected unweighted graph $G$

quote_B.text: answering affirmatively the general factor question for unimodular random graphs

notes: Second result: invariant strongly Rayleigh / determinantal processes on any countable group are factors of IID (StronglyRayleighDPP Lean). Prior partial results (transient graphs, amenable settings, Timár).

claim_formal: ∀ bounded smooth simply connected D (two marked points), triangular-lattice approximations: uniform odd integer Lipschitz heights h_δ ⇒ ḡ + σΦ_D (Dirichlet GFF); similarly weighted integer heights ∀x∈[1/√2,1] and uniform real Lipschitz heights ⇒ multiple of GFF, with tuned-boundary interface ⇒ SLE_4

quote_A.text: converges to a universal multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field

quote_B.text: Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice, resolving Schramm's Problem 2.3.

notes: Schramm's problem collection (Problems 2.2 and 2.3), hence P3. Problem 2.3 (real heights: GFF plus SLE4) is resolved in full; for Problem 2.2 (integer heights) only the field part is resolved (O5 for that one). The summary leads with the integer models, so the headline choice is ambiguous.

claim_formal: ∀ (J,U) on the critical Ashkin–Teller line (incl. 4-state Potts), ∀ bounded Jordan D, ∀ admissible approximations: (H_δ, C^w_δ, C^f_δ, C_∂,δ) ⇒ (h/(π√g), C^w, C^f, A_{−a,a}(h)) jointly in law (GFF and its recursive two-valued local sets)

quote_A.text: The height converges to a Gaussian free field with the predicted coupling constant, and the clusters converge to canonical recursive two-valued local sets of that same field.

quote_B.text: This is the height and current-cluster assertion formulated by Alcalde L\'opez, Heeney, and Lis \cite[Conjecture~1.2]{AlcaldeLopezHeeneyLis2026}.

notes: Scaling-limit identification coded M9. At U=0 (double random currents) the result was partly known (Duminil-Copin–Lis–Qian).

claim_formal: ∀ deterministic spectra Λ_N with μ_N ⇒ μ compactly supported and extreme eigenvalues → support edges, U_N Haar on O(N): lim E P_N = lim P_N (a.s.) = F(μ) = inf_{p} {S(p)+G_1(p)}, at every fixed temperature

quote_A.text: \lim_{N\to\infty}\E P_N =\lim_{N\to\infty}P_N =\mathcal F(\mu) :=\inf_{p\in\cP}\{S(p)+G_1(p)\}

quote_B.text: We solve this problem for every fixed temperature when the limiting spectral law is compactly supported and there are no asymptotic outliers.

notes: Earlier rigorous formulas needed high-temperature conditions, so O8 is an alternative. Corollaries: the pressure with external fields and the zero-field ground-state energy. Lean (InvariantIsing; the main theorem was truncated in the input, checked in ComparatorChallenges) states the limiting pressure plus field and ground-state variants.

claim_formal: ∀ k≥3, ∃ α_k∈(0,∞): lim_{n→∞} P(random k-SAT with ⌊cn⌋ uniformly signed proper clauses is satisfiable) = 1 if c<α_k, 0 if c>α_k

quote_A.text: there is a constant \(\alpha_k\in(0,\infty)\) such that, for independent proper uniformly signed \(k\)-clauses sampled with replacement

quote_B.text: We credit Gaia Carenini [[5]](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/229/) with priority for resolving the satisfiability conjecture. This paper gives an alternative proof

notes: Satisfiability threshold conjecture. Priority is credited to Carenini's concurrent ECCC TR26-229, so O9 per rule 9 (O1 if concurrent independent work is treated as settling). Additional new results: Var(hitting time)=Θ_k(n) and computability of α_3. Lean FixedClauseThreshold matches.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3, ∀ β≥0: free zero-field Ising measure μ_{d,β} on the d-regular tree is a factor of IID ⇔ tanh β ≤ (d−1)^{−1/2}

quote_A.text: the free zero-field Ising law $\mu_{d,\beta}$ is a factor of IID in the sense of \eqref{eq:equivariance} if and only if \[ \tanh\beta\le(d-1)^{-1/2}. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the positive implication, including equality, resolving the conjecture of Nam, Sly and Zhang; the strict converse is known.

notes: Exact threshold coded M9 (M5 'iff' alternative). The converse direction was already known. Summary also calls this the ferromagnetic case of Lyons's question.

claim_formal: ∀ δ,k>0 ∃ C,n_0 ∀ n≥n_0: uniform n-step honeycomb SAW γ satisfies n^{3/4−δ} ≤ diam(γ) ≤ n^{3/4+δ} (and local mass/covering exponent 4/3) with probability ≥ 1 − C n^{−k}

quote_A.text: For uniform self-avoiding walks of every sufficiently large integer length on the honeycomb lattice, we prove diameter exponent 3/4

quote_B.text: Proves the diameter form of Nienhuis's predicted three-quarter exponent

notes: Flory/Nienhuis ν=3/4 prediction. Only the honeycomb lattice and the diameter form are covered (O5 alternative if the prediction is taken for all planar lattices or for scaling limits). Lean comparators are auxiliary estimates (strip mass, bridge finiteness, free energy), hence different.

claim_formal: ∃ w (absolute number of coordinate sweeps): ∀ε>0 ∃ d_0 ∀ d≥d_0 ∀ initial deck τ: TV(Thorp shuffle law after w·d shuffles on 2^d cards, uniform) ≤ ε; with lower bound 2d−O(1), so t_mix = Θ(log N)

quote_A.text: We prove that the Thorp shuffle on $`2^d`$ cards mixes in $`\Theta(d)`$ complete shuffles.

quote_B.text: settling its optimal mixing order for power-of-two deck sizes

notes: Record: Morris's O(d^44) → O(d^3) bounds; the optimal order (discussed in Jonasson's notes) is now determined, so rule 7 gives O1 with M9 (sharp order, not a sharp constant; M8 or O7 are alternatives if only constants count). N=2^d only. Lean BinarySweep encodes only the upper bound (∃w, eventually TV≤ε), hence weaker.

claim_formal: P(det A_n = 0) = (1/2+o(1))^n for the n×n symmetric matrix with iid uniform ±1 entries on and above the diagonal; for fixed p≠1/2, lim P(det A_n^{(p)}=0)^{1/n} = p²+(1−p)²

quote_A.text: \Pr(\det A_n=0)=\left(\frac12+o(1)\right)^n =2^{-n+o(n)}

quote_B.text: Determines the sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices

notes: Prefix ℙ for a probability asymptotic about a random matrix ('none' is an alternative, since the statement concerns one specified model). The posed problem is the conjectured sharp rate for symmetric Bernoulli matrices, where earlier work gave e^{−cn} bounds; P4 is an alternative, still O1/M9 under rule 7.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite cardinal λ, ∃ μ(λ)≥λ, ∀ AEC K with LS(K)≤λ: (∃ κ≥μ(λ) with K categorical in κ) → (∀ κ'≥μ(λ), K categorical in κ')

quote_A.text: For every infinite cardinal $\lambda$ there is a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)\ge\lambda$ such that the following holds for every AEC $K$ with $\LS(K)\le\lambda$

quote_B.text: We prove Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes in ZFC.

notes: M2 is an alternative because the core is the existence of a threshold μ(λ). Secondary result: under CH, an AEC refuting the prescribed Hanf threshold ℶ_{(2^{ℵ0})^+}, so that form is not ZFC-provable. Lean covers only the CH obstruction, hence different.

claim_formal: ¬∃ π ∈ Aut(D_T, ≤_T) with π ≠ id  (equivalently ∀π∈Aut(D_T) ∀a: π(a)=a)

quote_A.text: Every order automorphism of the full Turing-degree structure is the identity

quote_B.text: resolving the rigidity conjecture for the Turing degrees positively

notes: Rigidity of one named structure, coded as non-existence of nontrivial automorphisms (M4). M1 with prefix ∀ (∀π ∀a π(a)=a) or M7 (Aut = 1) are plausible alternatives.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥1, ∀ r.e. S⊆ℕ^n, ∃ m, ∃ P∈ℤ[A,W_1..W_m]: ∀ a∈ℕ^n, #{w∈ℕ^m : P(a,w)=0} = 1 if a∈S, 0 otherwise

quote_A.text: Every recursively enumerable set of natural-number tuples has a polynomial Diophantine representation with exactly one complete auxiliary tuple for each member.

quote_B.text: This proves the single-fold conjecture and, consequently, the finite-fold conjecture.

notes: Corollary: Hilbert's 10th problem stays undecidable under an at-most-one-solution promise.

claim_formal: ∃ query Q on finite τ-structures (τ = eight binary relations; 𝔽_3 linear-system consistency): Q is isomorphism-invariant and PTIME-decidable, and Q is not definable in full CPT with counting; hence CPT+C does not capture PTIME

quote_A.text: A linear-consistency query over 𝔽3 in a fixed binary vocabulary is decidable in polynomial time but not in the full counting formalism.

quote_B.text: confirming the noncapture conjecture of Blass, Gurevich and Shelah

notes: Expressive-power separation (a logic does not capture a complexity class) coded M10 over M4. Second result: witnessed symmetric choice strictly extends CPT+C. Lean main theorem (checked in ComparatorChallenges, truncated in the input) matches.

claim_formal: Con(ZF) → Con(ZF + PP + AC_WO + ¬AC)

quote_A.text: If $\ZF$ is consistent, then so is $\ZF+\PP+\ACwo+\neg\AC$.

quote_B.text: We prove that the Partition Principle does not imply the Axiom of Choice

notes: Posed question: does PP imply AC in ZF? Since ZFC proves PP, non-implication means PP→AC is independent of ZF, hence O4; O2 ('no' to the question, per the H10-over-ℚ convention) is the alternative. Lean PartitionConsistency.main_consistency matches (main theorem truncated in the input, checked in ComparatorChallenges).

claim_formal: ∀ pure type system P: (∀ legal expression in every valid context, weakly β-normalizing) → (all such strongly β-normalizing)

quote_A.text: We prove that every weakly β-normalizing pure type system is strongly β-normalizing.

quote_B.text: This resolves the β-Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀ hyperbolic group G with ∂G ≅ S²: ∃ ρ: G → Isom(ℍ³) with proper cocompact action and finite kernel

quote_A.text: There is a homomorphism $\rho:G\to\Isom(\HH^3)$ for which the action on $\HH^3$ is proper and cocompact. Its kernel is finite.

quote_B.text: This resolves Cannon's conjecture positively.

notes: Corollary: a torsion-free such G is π1 of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold.

claim_formal: ∃ infinite group G with an ordinary finite presentation, residually finite, every element of finite 2-power order

quote_A.text: There exists an infinite residually finite group with an ordinary finite presentation in which every element has finite 2-power order.

quote_B.text: answering the finitely presented Burnside question negatively

notes: Counterexample to the universal question 'is every f.p. periodic group finite?' (rule 5 → M3). Companion results: an infinite f.p. periodic Kazhdan group St_12(R), and f.p. nil/radical non-nilpotent 𝔽2-algebras answering the nilpotence and Kurosh-type questions negatively. Lean PeriodicGroup states only infinite f.p. periodic (no residual finiteness or 2-power order), hence weaker.

claim_formal: Thompson's group F is not amenable (no F-invariant mean exists)

quote_A.text: Thompson's group \(F\) is not amenable.

quote_B.text: This confirms Geoghegan's conjecture and resolves the amenability problem for F.

notes: Also describable as P2 (the amenability problem for F). Under the H10 convention that would make it O2 (the question 'is F amenable?' gets the answer no), but against Geoghegan's conjecture it is O1.

claim_formal: ∃ finitely generated residually finite group G with cd(G)=2 and gd(G)=3 (no 2-dimensional K(G,1))

quote_A.text: There is a finitely generated residually finite group $G$ such that \[ \cdim G=2,\qquad \gdim G=3. \]

quote_B.text: disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

notes: Explicit witness (height kernel in a RAAG); per rule 1 the prefix is still ∃.

claim_formal: ∀ finitely generated group G: G has decidable word problem ⇔ G embeds in a finitely presented simple group

quote_A.text: For every finitely generated group \(G\), the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(G\) has decidable word problem. \item \(G\) embeds in a finitely presented simple group.

quote_B.text: We prove the Boone–Higman conjecture.

notes: The direction 'embeds ⇒ decidable WP' was classical (Boone–Higman). Strengthenings: type-F∞ simple overgroups, and a universal F∞ group containing every f.p. group.

claim_formal: ∀ discrete group G: G amenable ⇔ every uniformly bounded representation of G on a Hilbert space is similar to a unitary one; for countable G also amenable ⇔ strongly Ulam stable

quote_A.text: A discrete group is amenable if and only if it is unitarizable.

quote_B.text: This resolves Dixmier's unitarizability problem affirmatively for discrete groups.

notes: Dixmier's problem: P1 is plausible if read as a conjecture. Amenable ⇒ unitarizable was classical, and the new direction is unitarizable ⇒ amenable. Second result: the converse to Kazhdan's theorem (strong Ulam stability characterizes amenability), answering Burger–Ozawa–Thom.

claim_formal: ∃ torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G that is not residually finite (and not linear over any field)

quote_A.text: There exists a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group that is not residually finite.

quote_B.text: answering the residual-finiteness question for hyperbolic groups negatively

notes: The question 'are all hyperbolic groups residually finite?' is answered by a counterexample (rule 5 → M3). It is often treated as a conjecture-level question (P1 possible).

claim_formal: ∃ group G: G infinite, finitely presented, simple and amenable

quote_A.text: There exists an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group.

quote_B.text: giving a positive answer to the finite-presentation existence question for simple amenable groups
